Severe Storm Batters New South Wales Community, Damaging Buildings and Toppling Trees

Severe Weather Hits Southern Tablelands

A violent, fast-moving storm struck the small rural community of Good Hope, located near Yass on the New South Wales Southern Tablelands. The severe weather system brought destructive winds, heavy lightning, and large hail, causing significant property damage but resulting in no reported injuries.

Local authorities and residents reported that the system arrived rapidly with little prior warning, leaving behind a trail of damaged structures and debris.

Property Damage and Local Impacts

According to the New South Wales State Emergency Service (SES), the storm caused widespread structural damage:

  • Roof Damage: Six roofs were entirely ripped off, while 10 other buildings sustained varying degrees of roof damage.
  • Debris and Trees: Strong winds toppled numerous trees, temporarily blocking road access to the affected area.
  • Infrastructure: Power lines were downed after a pergola roof was blown into a utility pole, resulting in an eight-hour power outage at a local holiday park.
  • Heavy Objects Moved: Extreme winds shifted large items, including a shipping container that traveled roughly 300 metres and collided with a horse float.

Eyewitness Accounts and Official Responses

Residents described the sudden weather event as unprecedented for the area. Yass Hilltops SES commander Deanne Young characterized the occurrence as a "tornado-like event," noting that a funnel cloud appeared to be forming during the storm.

Local councillor and resident David Rothwell recounted the intense lightning and golf-ball-sized hail that pounded windows and roofs. Good Hope Resort owner Elizabeth Richardson-Szabo expressed relief that no injuries occurred despite the severity of the damage.

Clean-Up Operations and Verification

Clean-up efforts commenced immediately and are expected to continue. Residents are currently working to clear debris, repair damaged structures, and restore normalcy.

To verify original announcements and safety updates, members of the public can consult official channels such as the NSW State Emergency Service (SES) or the Bureau of Meteorology (BOM) for ongoing weather warnings and emergency advice.
